axis_a_operate_today.name: Cold-start orientation and repo map
evidence: README describes Click; docs/contributing.md lists development notes; docs/ contains user and contributor documentation.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: The project purpose and broad layout are easy to identify.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Setup and environment contract
evidence: pyproject.toml declares Python >=3.10, dependency groups, tox envs, uv.lock; .devcontainer/on-create-command.sh creates .venv and installs development dependencies.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: Runtime and dependency contract is explicit through uv/tox and devcontainer.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Locality of infrastructure and external dependency exposure
evidence: No database, queue, cache, object store, auth provider, payment, or remote service required by pyproject/test configuration.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: Proof is mostly local Python execution.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Harness front door and command discoverability
evidence: pyproject.toml exposes tox envs and pytest configuration; CI runs uv/tox; no .harness front door existed before this run.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: Commands are discoverable but diffuse across pyproject, docs, and CI rather than one canonical harness verb.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Boot and health/readiness path
evidence: tox env_run_base runs pytest; CI invokes uv run --locked --no-default-groups --group dev tox run.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: Tests are a practical health check for a library, but no dedicated boot/doctor command existed before harness setup.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Seed, fixture, reset, and cleanup state
evidence: tests/conftest.py provides CliRunner; tests use runner.invoke and isolated filesystem/tmp mechanisms.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: State needs are light and test-local; there is no separate seed/reset command, mostly because persistent state is not central.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Supported interaction surfaces
evidence: Click is itself a CLI toolkit; tests exercise commands with CliRunner.invoke; examples/ contains example CLIs.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: Agents can exercise real CLI behavior through the same public surfaces tests use.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Existing deterministic back-pressure sensors
evidence: pytest, tox, ruff, pre-commit, mypy, pyright, coverage configuration, GitHub Actions test/pre-commit/typing workflows.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: Multiple deterministic sensors exist locally and in CI.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Observability and evidence artifacts
evidence: pytest output, exit codes, coverage config, stdout/stderr assertions in tests.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: Evidence is mostly terminal output and test assertions; no first-class JSON run report/artifact path is documented for local runs.

axis_a_operate_today.name: Compounding harness loop
evidence: No pre-existing .harness governance, retrospectives, or difficulty ledger in the clone.
axis_a_operate_today.notes: The repo had strong engineering checks but no explicit harness-retro improvement loop before this flow.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Structural coupling and blast radius
evidence: src/click/ is a compact library package with focused modules such as core.py, types.py, parser.py, testing.py.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: Single package topology keeps blast radius understandable.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Temporal/change coupling
evidence: Deep git co-change mining was skipped in static mode.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: Temporal coupling was not proven; defaulted weak rather than inferred strong.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Cohesion and locality of change
evidence: Tests are grouped by behavior area under tests/test_*.py near the src/click package.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: Feature behavior and tests are navigable by topic.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Seams, substitution, and dependency inversion
evidence: click.testing.CliRunner and pytest fixture in tests/conftest.py provide a reusable command invocation seam.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: The test harness exposes a strong seam for CLI behavior.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Hermetic, offline, and isolated testability
evidence: pytest tests operate on local Python code and use CliRunner/tmp isolation; no remote service dependency was detected.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: Useful proof can run offline after dependencies are available.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Side-effect isolation and external-effect sinks
evidence: CLI tests capture stdout/stderr and use isolated filesystem patterns; no risky external side effects detected.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: Side effects are mostly local process/file/terminal effects and are capturable.

axis_b_adaptability.name: State evolution and consequence verification
evidence: Tests assert outputs, exceptions, exit codes, and local file interactions for CLI behavior.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: State consequence verification exists for CLI/file outcomes, but no broader fixture lifecycle is needed or encoded as a harness command.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Architecture boundary enforceability
evidence: ruff, mypy, pyright, and import convention linting are configured.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: Static checks exist, but explicit architecture boundary rules are not visible.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Complexity, size, and navigability thresholds
evidence: ruff and type checkers are configured; package is relatively compact.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: General static quality gates exist; complexity-specific thresholds were not found.

axis_b_adaptability.name: Inner-loop speed and repeatability
evidence: pytest/tox lanes are local and repeatable; uv.lock pins dependencies.
axis_b_adaptability.notes: The loop is repeatable, but first-run dependency environment setup can dominate time.
